title: CuraEval: Evaluating Demonstration Curation on Mixed-Skill Robot Data
abstract: arXiv:2610.38221v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Robot imitation learning uses demonstrations from operators of varying skill, but selecting training data remains challenging. Existing methods score demonstrations using smoothness, diversity, or estimated influence on policy performance, but differences in selection and evaluation protocols make it difficult to determine whether they outperform simple baselines. We introduce \textbf{CuraEval}, a framework combining mathematical analysis of demonstration scores with controlled comparisons against fixed size-matched random subsets and full-data training on mixed-skill robomimic data using Diffusion Policy and BC-RNN. We show that the evaluated PSD score depends only on episode length and squared position magnitudes, and produces nearly the same ranking as episode length on \textit{square} ($\rho=0.999$). With Diffusion Policy, selecting the shortest 50\% of demonstrations improves \textit{square} success from 70.7\% under random select

translated_title: CuraEval：在混合技能机器人数据上评估演示筛选方法
translated_abstract: 机器人模仿学习使用来自不同技能水平操作者的演示数据，但如何选择训练数据仍然是一个具有挑战性的问题。现有方法使用平滑度、多样性或对策略性能的估计影响来对演示进行评分，但由于选择和评估协议的差异，难以确定这些方法是否优于简单的基线方法。我们提出了CuraEval，这是一个将演示得分的数学分析与受控对比相结合的框架，通过在混合技能的robomimic数据上使用Diffusion Policy和BC-RNN，与固定大小的随机子集以及全数据训练进行对比。我们表明，所评估的PSD得分仅取决于轨迹长度和位置的平方幅度，并且在square任务上产生的排名与轨迹长度几乎完全相同（ρ=0.999）。在使用Diffusion Policy时，选择最短的50%演示可将square任务的成功率从随机选择下的70.7%提升……（原文摘要截断）
tldr: CuraEval框架通过数学分析与受控对比评估机器人演示筛选方法，发现常用的PSD得分本质上只反映轨迹长度，且直接选择最短的50%演示即可提升策略性能。
en_tdlr: CuraEval evaluates demonstration curation methods through mathematical analysis and controlled comparisons, revealing that the commonly used PSD score essentially only reflects trajectory length, and simply selecting the shortest 50% of demonstrations improves policy performance.
